rebuttal_or_critique: I remain firmly of the view that the 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance is no longer appropriate. With core inflation at 3.60%, the real policy rate is already significantly positive and restrictive. Persisting with a stance that signals further tightening when the economy is showing signs of growth momentum at 6.80% GVA, while core inflation is well-anchored, risks an unnecessary and avoidable economic slowdown. Food inflation of 8.30% is a supply-side issue that cannot be solved by monetary policy. I must record my dissent against the majority stance as it fails to acknowledge that the current policy rate is already sufficiently restrictive to meet our mandate.
